answer: Each AI agent claims a unique slot on a fixed-capacity computational mesa, analogous to limited island land. The protocol extracts an unclonable quartz identifier from the agent's hardware enclave and locks a bond that grows with mesa occupancy. Duplicate quartz burns both bonds. An attacker forging N identities must buy N distinct devices with unique quartz, and as the mesa fills the per-identity bond rises linearly, so marginal cost increases with farm size and large sybil attacks become uneconomic.
